newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE COFFEE ENDS DOWN IN SYMPATHY WITH NEW YORK.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE COFFEE ENDS DOWN IN SYMPATHY WITH NEW YORK.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures headed lower in sympathy with the New York market as funds and commission houses rolled nearby positions amid a perception of ample supply, traders said on Wednesday.
The September/November spread widened its discount, mainly as a result of September's continued weakness as non-trade players baled out of the position and into further forward months.
"All day it's been fund and commission house rollovers and for once it's actually following New York," said one trader.
"There's plenty of (robusta) coffee around...and even if it doesn't pass grading, people still feel it's marketable," he said.
At the close September stood $10 lower at $1,510 while second-month November was considered more expensive at $1,529, down $8 on the day. Volume totalled 5,496 lots.
Absence of roaster demand weakened the support base, although some price fixing from trade bargain-hunters was seen on a scale basis to limit the slide.
"The problem is that there are no roasters willing to go in and buy it -- they're well covered," he said.
In fundamental news, Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation said 946,000 60-kg bags of coffee were harvested in July compared to 622,000 bags in the same month last year.
The federation said Colombia's coffee exports, including federation and private exporters, totalled 804,000 bags in July compared to 894,000 in the same month last year.
